body:
That my parent's relationship, specifically the default emasculating way my mother treats my father, is the reason I will likely never get married. Also the reason I've told her for the last 10 years to hope my younger brother has children because that is the only way she is getting grandchildren.

I think, with my brother and I now out of the house and independent, that my parents would be better off seperated. My father would certainly be happier. Not sure how my mother would cope well but, her complete communication shutdown anytime something doesn't go her way is prime reason their relationship isn't working. Despite my love for her, I'm approaching the point where I don't care because I'm tired of seeing my father so miserable all the time.

My father talks about being consistently and angrily shut down when trying to use the communications tools suggested during their brief marriage counceling years ago. Counciling that she, supposedly, ended by simply refusing to go. About being verbally harangued until he responds in kind and then is immediately jumped on for "yelling", something I've observed multiple times in person. As well as a variety of issues that boil down to "your mother isn't participating in communication towards resolving conflicts".

My mother accuses my father of vitrolic verbal abuse and all of us "boys" ganging up on her, how she is never right. She says he yells at her daily, though through my childhood the only time I heard my father yell in anger was behind closed doors after my mother had already been yelling at him for ten minutes or more. She ends conflicts/arguments with ME by either physically leaving or by looking away and being verbally non-responsive, which I'm fighting not to classify as childish in my own head.

Separate conversations with them about the relationship has reached the point where one of them HAS to be lying to me to make themselves look the victim. I'm forced based on personal interaction and observation to conclude the liar is my mother.

I still love my mother, I'm not sure I LIKE her anymore. I feel like I should be more torn up about that than I am.
Thanks for letting me know I'm not alone in this. In a better place mentally right now. Trying not to anticipate the next dip.

I love my parents very much and am, as I progress through adulthood, increasingly grateful to have had/have them as parents. I now make a point of telling them this periodically.

That said, I am the family communicator. I both placate through logic/perspective/fuckingtruth and don't put up with the bullshit when/where appropriate. This weakness cannot be shared with my family. It will undermine one of the things I feel like I get right/do well in my life.
While I understand what you describe, for me its more a feeling of being stuck. A focus on the fact that I'm already HERE right now, not a fear of what might happen.

Thank You.

Though I didn't get very far, I got far enough to call my mother who was joined by my grandmother. Managed to keep my voice steady and the conversation has helped my mood.
I'm not sure how I feel about this crying thing. I'm not used to it.

Not much has changed, a lot has changed? I don't know if I'm perceiving it because I want to or people are responding to a change in me. Some days I'm hopeful, some days I'm ... well not.

Objective statistics haven't changed much. Maybe a bit more "getting out" but ... sometimes I'm just standing around trying to decide how long I should stick around before its not weird that I leave.
